## Design

### 2026-10-08 – I started the work for this journal entry about 2 days ago. I worked on copying the PCB from the tutorial and modifying it. (*I didn't submit this journal entry earlier due to me thinking I could subm

**11h**

I started the work for this journal entry about 2 days ago. I worked on copying the PCB from the tutorial and modifying it. (*I didn't submit this journal entry earlier due to me thinking I could submit an entry on the StarbieZ project page and not the home page.)
I spent the whole day, and I quite probably went past 4 hours (the actual making time from the tutorial) to include the things that would make it my own.
The screenshot below shows the base schematic and there will be progression along the way of this entry a lot further from the typical tutorial board!

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 060906](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/fae767970b416d1df43ed744b85a578a3d193119aa3f3c684b5e8a30ff5deb39.png)

I then laid out my PCB, creating the `Edge.Cuts` star from a reference image I found on Google first (by searching up "pixel star", thanks Icons8):

![pixel-star](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/7ff8605c9e731413f516d03cfce92301dbd87498d7489d86d6314153a5ed8859.jpg)

I traced it by the pixel to get it into the project, though the grid settings were stuffing me up a little and I think I spent 40 minutes trying to trace it sufficiently.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/eb9082c5efbece2387600fcd5b03fdeb166d3ffe93d21456692fcefdac3b7463.png)

I then meticulously traced out the ground plane by dragging the corners where they needed to be... (I know I could've just drew a square across the whole PCB and clicked B, I realized that after the fact!!) Oh yeah, and I almost forgot, *Microsoft Family Safety* kept prompting me to sign in to Microsoft services and wouldn't go away, I just disabled the parental controls service permanently because I got so frustrated (sorry Dad.)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/0a92614fcc35199c9a212caef092517e29f98f42750182cf383ed6afddcdeb0d.png)

I took a bold move after the 4 hours and 5 minutes mark, deciding to change the MCU. (spoiler: And it quickly spiraled to an ESP32-S3 Plus because I had the idea to make it expandible by the person..)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/9c4e0a1e2a026ecd06e762904896d639231463d376be26a9a31a28dfc3f4748c.png)

That swap over from the ESP32-C3 didn't take very long because the great thing with Seeed Studio XIAOs is they make them all extremely similar in structure. :)

Anyway, the next stupid thing I did was I chose to include an LDR for sensing light levels. It can be guessed that I also messed this one up bad and it set me back trying to find the correct new part, if you did guess that you are correct.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 084634](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/ae0bab20b8b292ccf1d1153bc29722810cfb1017c7f1ad4efe12d1ef578e4901.png)

I put it on the right wing of the star PCB due to the ease of access to HEAPS of analog pins on that side, and I just had to measure analog signals, there was no other way out. I also added a third switch button, not thinking about clearance clearly (I'm such a goofball... and yet again, I would come to realize this later.)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/697f86e7e721de6a3bd002798bafe2137013d5f8ed1000bd376dc28059eaef58.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/4dd2723da12722abadce18d396238ca1e042c7a237a4330aaf16150b68c79445.png)

A lot of organization, and another output was added to the project. A buzzer (or a piezo) was heavily inspired by the Sprig's design when I made my Columns game for them (still waiting for approval on that one), and I feel this Tamagotchi would do really well with a bit of tunes while flicking through the menu. (It's also an improvement in the matter of accessibility!)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/c67159942839ed55a0d0af6bf85433883b89b51b3e420d110995304859a12fde.png)

I made some space in the star by increasing the area and I put it at the bottom of the board, and I even included a mini 100 ohm resistor on the side.. (it's R4!) I didn't want to choose SMD for debugging purposes, but I found SMD components are considerably better after routing traces to the XIAO...

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/49646cee691d686752a6f031cb1ab360056d9422f2c187c7c0356ce9a98e11b4.png)

After figuring out how to import *some* 3D models into the footprints, I found a honeycomb SVG icon on Flaticon (wow, cool name) that I really liked and I put it at the two bottom corners of the star. (PLEASE [!!] ignore the silkscreen warnings in DRC, they don't matter in this project about fab and production for this reason..)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/eed04180fe1ac47ce4197d38704f4eea1e2196b9fd2d0e8b5432745211d18904.png)

(I'm a time-blind perfectionist writing this journal entry, sorry it's so long)

Around this time was the point I realized the 3rd switch had no clearance around the 6-axis IMU, and this was right after the switch to the ESP32-S3 Plus... so I expanded the area of my PCB yet again by a *slight bit* to fit the switch further down the star into its leg. I decided to place the buzzer against the screen so the GPIO header would be allowed free space. This is the chonkiness coming through :P

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/d85f01b48b460d5941d93a71c61bb63a0765bbf2d1bae94fef0012e9475364aa.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/a093de1bade53cf7160ca0ba56aea19f6f78ad43383289f7c45d5489bae538dc.png)

After this, I shut off the computer for the day and kept pondering in anxiety about whether I chose the right LDR. Turns out, as I would find out on Wednesday morning, the LDR I had chosen was completely off the market. I could not find it anywhere because its datasheet was *that* old. Yikes...

I done a little more research, switched the LDR to a generic one on KiCAD and documented my choice: the GL5528. I chose this because I found the dark resistance was around what I expected had been with 10 megaohms. I also switched out the 10 kilohm fixed resistor with an 100 kilohm one, so that the voltage I'd read in software would be a little more stable.

I asked Claude Sonnet 4.6 to make a scattered star SVG for me (because who creates SVGs by hand in plain text? I'm no graphic designer...) and I chose to put it on every corner of the star! I tested it inside JLCPCB and it looks ***SO*** cool when the PCB is white and the silkscreen is black, it makes this look like a professionally made product...!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/adb8e815f358caddb1ea74f3f587d57d6de0a365d11ada8568fe6d91a00766ca.png)

![sm_white_top 3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5L83T8pgt4C0kG6QB6wl2GpFHsDV2Xmw/f8f49ab5e6d6e6c941f6e0790248aa19f8a3f71b6d20e04adb0e499a8579588c.png)

I put more techy explanation stuff in my GitHub repository, but this is the more personal journal entry. I'm kind of proud of myself as this is my second PCB ever, though I'm going to have a little trouble with just $30 funding. If anyone could help make this project more possible, I'd really appreciate it. Thanks for reading me rambling on! :3

I'll be working on the software for the next few days, I have lots planned that I'll journal in the GitHub instead of here because Hack Club Half-Life counts Hackatime hours into the final result. I'm just being fair...
